newsitem.title: UK: DMG chairman John Craven to resign end-May.
newsitem.headline: DMG chairman John Craven to resign end-May.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, said on Tuesday its chairman Sir John Craven planned to retire, but stressed it was not related to recent problems in the firm's fund management arm.

"I can confirm that Sir John Craven will retire from his position as chairman of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell at the end of May and join the advisory board of the Deutsche Bank group," DMG spokesman Markus Will told Reuters.

DMG said Craven's retirement "has nothing whatsoever to do with the Peter Young affair as speculated in the press today". DMG's fund management arm, Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, is expected to be severely disciplined shortly by British investment watchdog IMRO for problems in three of its funds which were managed by Peter Young.

Fund manager Young was sacked by MGAM last September following the uncovering of irregularities in the funds. Young, who has said he is not guilty of any criminal activity, is currently under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office.
The episode has been an embarrassing and costly one for DMG, which has aggressively been building up its investment banking business with the aim of becoming one of a handful of truly global firms.

Craven, 56, was chief executive of Morgan Grenfell from 1987 to 1989 when he was made chairman of the group. Earlier this month British conglomerate Lonrho Plc said Craven would take over as chairman from John Leahy. This appointment takes effect from Wednesday.
